q: 1. Latest start time is the
options: latest time by which an activity can be started without delaying the project
latest time by which an activity can be completed without delaying the project
latest time the event can occur
explain: Latest Start Time (LST) is the maximum delay possible for the start of a task that won't push back the project completion date.

q: 2. The interrelationship between the functional elements of a programme is achieve through
explain: A work breakdown structure shows how the elements of a programme relate.

q: 3. If a is the optimistic time, b is the pessimistic time and m is the most likely time, then the average time is equal to
explain: The formula for expected (average) time in a Beta distribution is t_e = (a + 4m + b) / 6.

q: 4. The difference between the total float and the free float is termed as
explain: Interfering float is the difference between Total Float and Free Float (TF - FF).

q: 5. An event is
options: a definite position of an activity
explain: Per the answer key, d. An event is an instant at which activities start or finish.

q: 6. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow a
explain: Individual activity durations in PERT are modeled using a unimodal Beta distribution curve.

q: 7. The independent float affects only
explain: By definition, independent float is the time by which an activity can be delayed without affecting any other activity in the network.

q: 8. The scheduled completion time of an operation in CPM chart is mentioned on
options: left top corner outside the circle
left top corner inside the circle
explain: Per the answer key, it is shown at the top left, outside the circle.

q: 9. The probability factor Z in PERT is given by
options: (scheduled time – earliest expected time) / standard deviation
(latest allowable time – scheduled time) / standard deviation
explain: Z = (TS – TE)/σ, where TS is the scheduled time and TE the earliest expected time.

q: 10. What are essential to draw CPM ?
explain: CPM is primarily a time-management tool; while resources are important, time estimates for each activity are the fundamental requirement for the network.

q: 11. Resource smoothening means
options: adjustment of resources to have the least variations
complete renovation if resources suit the requirement
optimization and economical utilization of resources
explain: Resource smoothening rearranges non-critical activities within their float to minimize fluctuations in resource demand while keeping project duration fixed.

q: 12. The latest allowable time for any event i is equal to
explain: During backward pass calculations, the Latest Allowable Occurring Time T_L for an event is computed as the minimum of (T_L^j - t^ij).

q: 13. Critical-path connecting the start and end events time wise is
explain: The critical path is the longest path through a network diagram; any delay on this path delays the entire project.

q: 14. In the time-cost optimization using CPM, the crashing of the activities along the critical path is done starting with the activity having
explain: Crashing begins with the activity having the least (lowest) cost slope, as it gives the maximum time reduction per unit extra cost.

q: 15. Float may be defined as the difference between
options: latest start time and the earliest start time
latest finish time and the earliest finish time
time available and the time required to complete the activity
explain: All three expressions give the float.

q: 16. Critical activities having total float are
explain: An activity is critical if its total float is zero, meaning there is no flexibility in its timing.

q: 17. When all the paths are arranged according to the descending order of the float, the path which is next to critical path is known as
explain: The path with the next-lowest float after the critical path (zero float) is termed the secondary critical path.

q: 18. Which of the following is a PERT event?
explain: An event is a milestone (a completion). The other options are ongoing activities.

q: 19. The activity which consumes maximum time is called a
explain: A single activity consuming a lot of time isn't 'called' a specific name in network theory; it is the 'path' that becomes critical.

q: 20. Of the following the PERT event is
explain: An event is a milestone (a completion point). 'Concrete cured' marks a completed state; the others are activities.

q: 21. The figure [merging arrows] indicates
explain: When multiple activity arrows point into a single event node, it is known as a merge event.

q: 22. In PERT analysis the actual performance of task is known is
explain: Per the answer key, b. Note: by standard definition the performance of a task is an activity, so the stem or key looks misprinted.

q: 23. The figure [bursting arrows] indicates
explain: When multiple activity arrows originate from a single event node, it is known as a burst event.

q: 24. In PERT analysis, the start and end of event is represented by
explain: Per the answer key, b (event).

q: 25. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known as
explain: The point in time marking the start or completion of an activity is called an event (represented by a node/circle).

q: 26. Free float is the
explain: Free float is a subset of total float; specifically, it is the portion of total float that can be used without delaying the next activity.

q: 27. An activity requires
explain: Every activity needs both time and resources.

q: 28. When all the paths are arranged according to the descending order of the float, the path which is next to the critical path is known as
explain: The path with the second-lowest amount of float (next to the critical path, which has zero float) is technically referred to in this context as the semi-critical path.

q: 29. A drawback of the bar chart is that
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind schedule
explain: Bar charts do not show the logical sequence or interdependence of activities.

q: 30. In CPM
options: time optimization is given prime importance
cost optimization is given prime importance
cost is directly proportional to time
explain: Unlike PERT (which is probabilistic and time-oriented), CPM is deterministic and focuses heavily on the trade-off between time and cost, prioritizing cost optimization.

q: 31. Milestones are
options: the events specifying the beginning and/or the end of subdivided activities
the stones indicating the distance along a highway
dates of important happenings in the history of any nation
explain: Milestones are key events marking the start or end of subdivided activities.

q: 32. Which method is known as minimum cost or maximum time schedule method
explain: CPM (Critical Path Method) is designed to find the schedule that minimizes total project cost by balancing direct and indirect costs over time.

q: 33. Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique around
explain: Henry Gantt developed the bar chart around 1900 (roughly 1910-1915).

q: 34. Critical path
explain: The critical path is the longest path through the network; therefore, it contains the activities with the least amount of flexibility or 'minimum slack' (usually zero).

q: 35. Milestone charts are developed around
explain: Per the answer key, 1940.

q: 36. Critical path is
explain: By definition, the critical path is the sequence of activities that takes the longest time to complete, determining the shortest possible project duration.

q: 37. For completion of a project, the CPM of the network represents
explain: The Critical Path Method identifies the minimum time required to complete the entire project based on the sequence of dependent tasks.

q: 38. Bar charts are suitable only for
explain: Per the answer key, a. Bar charts cannot show complex interdependencies, so they suit small projects.

q: 39. PERT is an abbreviation for
options: pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT = Programme (Program) Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 40. Henry Gant developed bar chart in
explain: Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique around 1900, well before CPM/PERT were developed.

q: 41. Expected project duration generally follows
explain: Per the answer key, a. The project duration is a sum of many activity times, so by the central limit theorem it is taken as normal. Activity times follow the beta curve.

q: 42. The difference between total float and free float is called interfering float which is nothing but the
explain: Interfering Float = Total Float - Free Float = Head Event Slack.

q: 43. Bar chart is suitable for
explain: Bar charts are simple and versatile, suitable for representing schedules of projects of all sizes - major and minor alike.

q: 44. The area under the β-distribution curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time divides the area into two equal halves, so there is a 50% chance on either side.

q: 45. Which of the following does not represent an activity?
options: The office area is being cleaned
explain: 'Site located' is a completed state (an event). The rest are ongoing tasks.

q: 46. Various activities of a project, are shown on bar charts by
explain: In a bar chart, each activity is represented by a horizontal bar/line whose length is proportional to its duration.

q: 47. The total cost verses time curve of an activity is
explain: The total cost curve is generally represented as a parabola or U-shaped because it is the summation of a decreasing indirect cost and an increasing direct cost curve.

q: 48. CPM stands for
explain: CPM = Critical Path Method.

q: 49. Which operation must complete first?
options: right of the line joining two circles
left of the line joining two circle
explain: In left-to-right network flow diagramming, the task on the left precedes and must be completed before downstream tasks.

q: 50. The first method invented for planning projects, was
explain: The bar chart (Gantt chart) method, invented in the late 1800s, was the earliest project planning tool, preceding milestone charts, CPM, and PERT.
